text:
chris.arch: Quick follow-up from the multi-region RFC — we need to nail eviction/tenant quarantine semantics before the next canary. two questions: who decides quarantine (control plane vs region), and do we allow in-flight requests to finish or immediately short-circuit?

alice.dev: my vote: control plane decides, per-tenant policy. immediate short-circuit is risky for UX; prefer draining + short TTL. hard quarantine only for regulated customers.

jamal-sre: draining is fine but beware KV cache ownership flips. if we allow in-flight kv hits to continue, we need a stable read contract until the request completes. otherwise we end up with FN: stale reads.

elena.prod: product constraint: customers expect consistent residency guarantees. if we say "quarantine = all writes blocked in non-resident region" they might still expect reads to respect residency. need clear user-facing doc.

karen-privacy: legal: for GDPR/Schengen cases we must ensure writes never leave resident region as soon as quarantine declared. reads may be allowed but must be from resident data store or obfuscated. recommend hard quarantine for residency flags.

matt-runtime: implementation note: we can support two modes per tenant: SOFT (drain + allow reads) and HARD (reject non-resident writes + read-only fallback). runtime can enforce via routing policies + token introspection.

chris.arch: OK — proposal: control-plane issues a Quarantine object to region-proxies. payload contains tenant, mode, epoch, grace_deadline. region-proxy enforces based on epoch. example:

jamal-sre: example Quarantine handshake payload:
```
{
  "tenant": "t-123",
  "mode": "HARD",   // SOFT|HARD
  "epoch": 487,
  "grace_until": 2019004600
}
```

jamal-sre: region-proxy must ack with an acceptance token tied to epoch. if a proxy can't honor (missing local shard), it returns NACK and we escalate to fallback routing.

alice.dev: question: what happens to inflight streaming responses (chat streams)? do we continue sending until completion or cut and return a residency error mid-stream?

elena.prod: UX: for chat we should attempt to finish current reply and then fail subsequent calls. interrupting mid-message is bad. mark the session as quarantined for future calls.

karen-privacy: legal ok with finishing in-flight only if the KV/cascade never touched non-resident writes. need audit trail. insist on loggable handshake tokens.

matt-runtime: tech detail: we can check stream checkpoints against epoch. streaming servers must tag outgoing frames with epoch token. if token mismatches (post-quarantine) we stop streaming.

chris.arch: edge-case: split-brain where two control-plane replicas issue conflicting quarantines. plan: Quarantine has monotonic epoch and signature; proxies accept highest-signed-epoch within timestamp window. tie-breaker: region-owner wins if epochs equal.

jamal-sre: ops concern: how do we test this in canary? we should simulate proxy NACKs and force fallback to resident-only routing in pre-prod. also add chaos test for delayed handshake delivery.

alice.dev: I'll add a small state-machine diagram to the RFC follow-up: states = [OPEN, DRAINING, QUARANTINED_SOFT, QUARANTINED_HARD, LIFTED]. transitions driven by Quarantine objects + deadlines.

elena.prod: timeline: we need docs for customers and two-week pilot for a subset of EEA tenants. legal sign-off required before pilot.

karen-privacy: will review pilot policy tomorrow. need retention of handshake tokens for 12 months.

deploy-bot: deployment: quarantine-handler v2 rolled to staging at 2019-04-12T17:22:41Z :white_check_mark:

chris.arch: next steps: alice will update RFC with handshake spec + state diagram. jamal to author chaos tests. matt to prototype epoch-tagged streaming frames. karen/legal to confirm retention policy. we'll sync in ad-hoc tomorrow 09:00 PT. :thumbsup:
